title: Build a short contemplative practice and examine its effects

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: A contemplative sequence can be executable without being beneficial every time. Record missed attempts, adverse effects and ordinary circumstances before interpreting a pattern; a short personal sequence is not a controlled causal study.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Five fictional opportunities: Monday three minutes, next task started with fewer interruptions; Tuesday missed because of necessary care; Wednesday three minutes, no noticeable change; Thursday stopped after one minute because focusing increased unease, then returned to an ordinary supported activity; Friday three minutes, next task interrupted by a delivery. No other observations exist.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Classify actual full, partial and missed practice. Compare the chosen next-task marker while preserving the adverse response and outside interruption. Choose a bounded next step.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A person completes a quiet pause but feels more agitated, then writes “successful because I finished.” What two dimensions must remain separate?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Three full attempts, one stopped attempt and one missed opportunity are recorded. Only Monday suggests improved fit; no causal effect or general calm is established. Do not repeat a distressing method to complete a quota. Partial: report only full attempts. Incorrect: call five planned occasions five completed practices or hide Thursday. A shorter or different ordinary practice, support or deferral can be appropriate.
criteria: Adverse and neutral outcomes remain visible
A short sequence does not establish causation

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: Completion and suitability differ. Retain both the performed sequence and adverse response; stop or change an unsuitable exercise and seek appropriate support for concerning distress. Finishing is not evidence of benefit.
